Cooking: 15 minutes
Total: 20 minutes | difficulty = 2 | image = | energy = | note = }} {{Recipe}} '''Kunun tamba''' is a porridge made from finger [[Cookbook:Millet|millet]]. It is common in the northern part of Nigeria. == Ingredients == *¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Millet|tamba (finger millet)]] *[[Cookbook:Ginger|Ginger]] *1 cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]] *1 cup [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] *2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] == Equipment == *[[Cookbook:Sieve|Sieve]] *Bowl *[[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|Pot]] == Procedure == #Wash the tamba and dry with a clean cloth. #Mix tamba with ginger. Grind the mixture until smooth. #Allow the ground mixture to cool down, then sieve the chaff to give a fine texture. #[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] water in a pot and add the tamba powder gradually, stirring gently to make a smooth mixture. #Add milk and sugar, then whisk until smooth and lump-free. == Notes, tips, and variations == *Finger millet porridge is usually prepared for babies as a weaning food. It is also eaten as [[Cookbook:Breakfast|breakfast]] in some regions. *Dilute with [[Cookbook:Water|water]] to get a thinner [[Cookbook:Porridge|porridge]] [[Category:Recipes using millet]] [[Category:Recipes using milk]] [[Category:Recipes using ginger]] [[Category:Nigerian recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using sugar]]

steps.text: Wash the tamba and dry with a clean cloth.
Mix tamba with ginger. Grind the mixture until smooth.
Allow the ground mixture to cool down, then sieve the chaff to give a fine texture.
Boil water in a pot and add the tamba powder gradually, stirring gently to make a smooth mixture.
Add milk and sugar, then whisk until smooth and lump-free.
